summary: This document extends DLEP with a credit window scheme aware of Diffserv, supporting both destination-specific and shared flow control. It builds on the base DLEP credit window mechanism.

eli5.summary: Each type of traffic gets its own set of tickets, so urgent items are not stuck behind slow ones.

questions: what is the dlep da credit extension
how does diffserv work with dlep credit windows
subtitle: A DLEP extension that ties credit-window flow control to destinations and Diffserv code points.

tldr.problem: DLEP has no flow control, and the credit window machinery of RFC 9893 needs an extension that says which traffic maps to which window.
tldr.mechanism: The Diffserv Aware Credit Window extension, Extension Type 6, uses the traffic classification and credit window mechanisms of RFC 9892 and RFC 9893. Windows are keyed on DLEP destinations and DSCPs, shared or dedicated, with a wildcard that matches any DSCP.
tldr.outcome: A router sends traffic to a modem only while credits are available in the matching window, and both sides can see mismatches in capability.

today: RFC 9894 is a Proposed Standard published in January 2026 and has not been obsoleted or updated. It relies on the messages and Data Items of RFC 9893.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
The Dynamic Link Exchange Protocol (DLEP, RFC 8175) exchanges link information between a modem and a router. The base specification has no flow control capability. This document defines an extension that gives a Diffserv-based flow control mechanism for traffic sent from a router to a modem.

Flow control uses one or more logical credit windows, each typically backed by a virtual or physical queue. The router uses traffic classification information from the modem to decide which traffic belongs to which window. An Ethernet-based version is in RFC 9895. When a flow has both Diffserv and Ethernet classification, the Ethernet information takes precedence, as RFC 9892 specifies.
sections.eli5: A router wants to send different kinds of traffic to a modem. This extension makes the modem give out separate tickets for each kind.

sections.title: The DA Credit Extension
sections.content:
The extension is called Diffserv Aware Credit Window, or DA Credit for short. It uses the traffic classification of RFC 9892 and the credit window flow control of RFC 9893. Readers should know both.

Windows are based on DLEP destinations and Differentiated Services Code Points (DSCPs, from RFC 2475). A window can be shared across traffic to several destinations and DSCPs, or used exclusively for a particular destination, DSCP, or both. The extension also supports a wildcard that matches any DSCP.
sections.eli5: Some tickets can be used by many kinds of traffic together. Others are reserved for one kind only.

sections.title: Turning the Extension On
sections.content:
An implementation indicates use of the extension by including the Diffserv Aware Credit Window Extension Type value in the Extensions Supported Data Item defined in RFC 8175. That value is 6.

An implementation that indicates this extension MUST support all message types, Data Items and the Diffserv Traffic Classification Sub-Data Item, along with the related processing in RFC 9892 and RFC 9893.

Extension Data Items MUST NOT be emitted by a DLEP participant unless its peer declared support in the initialization message it sent.
sections.eli5: Both sides must say they know how to play this game before either one starts using the special tickets.

sections.title: Management Considerations
sections.content:
Use of the extension SHOULD be configurable on both modems and routers, by a proprietary command-line interface or a YANG module. The YANG module definition is out of scope. Modems SHOULD support configuring the mapping from a DSCP to a credit window (queue), and MAY support configuring how many credit windows to advertise.

Routers may have limits on queues, and per-destination queues might not be supported at all. If the modem offers more than the router can handle, the router SHOULD use a subset of the windows. Alternatively it MAY reset the session and indicate that the extension is not supported. Either way, the mismatch SHOULD be reported to the user, for example by a user interface message or error logging.

If credit windows are in use, the router MUST NOT send traffic to the modem when credits are not available.
sections.eli5: If the router cannot handle all the ticket jars the modem offers, it uses just some of them and tells a person about the problem.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The extension reuses DLEP and the credit window mechanisms of RFC 9892 and RFC 9893, so their security considerations apply. It is exposed to threats like those against existing DLEP messages. One example is an injected message that resizes a credit window to a value that causes denial of service. The security mechanisms of RFC 8175 apply equally.

Wildcards are convenient for matching many flows, but could inadvertently match unexpected flows or new flows that appear after the wildcard was set up. The RFC says it is RECOMMENDED that wildcards not be used unless needed.
sections.eli5: A catch-all label is handy but may grab packages you did not mean it to. Use it only when you really need it.

sections.title: IANA Assignment
sections.content: IANA assigned one code point in the Extension Type Values registry, in the Dynamic Link Exchange Protocol (DLEP) Parameters registry group: code 6, Diffserv Aware Credit Window. The RFC defines no new messages or Data Items of its own.
sections.eli5: The official list of extension numbers got one new entry, number 6, for this extension.
